messages:
dana: kicking off a canary for ganymede21b (int4) on dedicated pool. seeing intermittent OOMs when batch_size >= 4 and requests with max_new_tokens >= 4096. 95p latency also ~20% higher than fp16. quality post-quant looks worse on our summarization set :frowning_face:
liam: can you drop the logs and the canary config? which quant recipe did we use? int4_8bit-kvprefetch?
dana: logs: <https://console.redwood.internal/canaries/2860501234|canary/2860501234>  (profile + heap traces attached). used recipe `ganymede21b-int4-v1` from model-catalog. repro script shows OOM pattern around token 3200 for multi-turn prompts.
zara: quick hypothesis: kv cache fragmentation + large per-batch max_new_tokens. for int4 we should tighten batch token budget and enable small-window prefetch. propose defaults: `max_batch_items: 3`, `max_batch_tokens: 2300`, and model default `max_new_tokens: 1024` for served routes.
zara: example patch config to try in canary (small):
```
route_config:
  model: ganymede21b-int4-v1
  defaults:
    max_new_tokens: 1024
  batching:
    max_batch_items: 3
    max_batch_tokens: 2300
  kv_prefetch: small_window
  fallback_on_oom: true
```
simon: fyi oncall note: we saw similar OOMs last month that were solved by bumping the kv-eviction_threshold and adding a warm-up reservation for the first 2 slots. memory fragmentation was high in those traces. suggest kv_eviction_threshold: 0.6 and reserved_slots: 2 for the canary.
alek: from QA: int4 shows a ~1.8 ROUGE-L drop on our summarization eval vs fp16 on the same prompt set. need to run eval-harness with the canary config to measure quality vs perf tradeoff. I can run two A/B runs if we have stable canary config.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Can canary be rolled with auto-fallback to fp16 on OOM? (yes/no)
ci-deploy: yes — we can push a canary with `fallback_on_oom: true` and route-level policy to rollback after 5 OOM events in 15m. I recommend starting with 2% traffic.
zara: also try lowering kv_prefetch window and enabling slot-compaction heuristic to reduce fragmentation during long sequences. small change may help tail-latency.
dana: plan: 1) apply zara's batching+defaults + simon's reservation + fallback flag; 2) run A/B for 24h at 2% traffic; 3) QA run (alek) on summarization + convo benchmarks; 4) collect perf/quality dashboard. I'll tag results here by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
qa-bot: queued eval job 48612 for ganymede21b-int4-v1 vs fp16. will post metrics when done.
liam: thanks — if we still see OOMs after those patches, let's try a canary with 8-bit quant (int8) or fall back to a mixed-precision variant for long-window routes.
dana: noted, will iterate. thanks all :pray:
